newsitem.title: UK: SmithKline's Hycamtin gets EU approval.
newsitem.headline: SmithKline's Hycamtin gets EU approval.

text.p: British drug giant SmithKline Beecham Plc said on Thursday that Hycamtin received final marketing approval in the 15 European Union member states for the treatment of relapsed ovarian cancer.
The company said Hycamtin, or topotecan HCI, would be available in most EU markets by early 1997.
Each year, about 28,000 new cases of ovarian cancer occur in the European Community, the company said.

SmithKline said a study showed that patients treated with Hycamtin demonstrated a higher response rate and a longer duration of response than patients treated with paclitaxel, a widely-used agent for the treatment of the disease.
In May, the drug received marketing clearance from the U.S. Food and Drug Administration for the treatment of patients with metastatic ovarian cancer after failure of chemotherapy.

Hycamtin, discovered by SmithKline scientists in the mid-1980s, is one of a new class of drugs that kill cancer cells by inhibiting the enzyme topoisomerase I in the human body. Drug resistance is a common problem in recurrent ovarian cancer because cancer cells frequently grow back with an increased resistance to existing treatments.
